title: 🏛️ Exams 2001–2021 · present simple or continuous in exam texts ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) A text on online shopping lists the problems customers face. Which form completes the next sentence? "Next, the issue of getting the correct size ___ a serious drawback when shopping for clothes and footwear online."
questions.explanation: The verb belongs to "the issue" (one thing), not to "clothes and footwear", which only come at the end of the sentence. The problem is a lasting fact, so the present simple is used, and a singular subject takes -s: remains. "remain" forgets the -s; "remaining" has no auxiliary, so it cannot be the verb of the sentence; "are remaining" agrees with the plural nouns at the end instead of with "the issue".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, general) A text about Earth Hour says what people do during the event. Which form completes the sentence? "People ___ in groups and have fun without using power."
questions.explanation: The text describes what happens during Earth Hour, so the present simple is used, as in "have fun" in the same sentence. "People" is plural: the verb has no -s. "gathers" adds an -s that only a singular subject takes; "gathering" needs be before it; "gathered" is a past form that does not fit a description in the present.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, technical) A text on safety at work gives advice to employees: "Follow the guidelines that your employer ___."
questions.explanation: The guidelines are a standing rule, so the verb is in the present simple, and "your employer" is one person: the verb takes -s, provides. "provide" forgets the -s; "providing" cannot be a verb without be; "are providing" uses a plural auxiliary with a singular subject.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2013, general) A text says that a bird called the passenger pigeon lived in North America a century ago and has now disappeared. Which form completes the sentence? "Today, there ___ not a single one left."
questions.explanation: "Today" asks for the present, and "not a single one" is singular, so the verb is is. "are" would need a plural; "was" is a past form, which does not go with "Today"; "has" cannot be followed by "not a single one left" without a past participle.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, technical) Two friends study at a technical school, and David is learning carpentry. Which word completes the sentence? "At the moment, his teacher ___ showing him how to plane wood in order to make doors."
questions.explanation: "At the moment" calls for the present continuous: be + verb in -ing. "His teacher" is one person, so the auxiliary is is. "are" does not agree with a singular subject; "has" would need a past participle (has shown), not -ing; "was" is past, which does not fit "At the moment".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, technical) A mother describes how her 15-year-old daughter uses the Internet every day. Which form completes the sentence? "She chats with her friends, ___ new films and reads newspapers and magazines."
questions.explanation: The sentence lists what she does regularly: "chats", ..., "reads" are in the present simple. The list keeps the same form for the same singular subject, so the verb takes -s: downloads. "download" forgets the -s; "downloaded" is past; "to download" is not a conjugated verb, so the list would lose a verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) A man says how he uses the Internet in his free time. Which form completes the sentence? "When I get home from work, I usually ___ my e-mail first."
questions.explanation: "usually" and "When I get home from work" describe a habit, which is told in the present simple. After "I", the verb takes no -s: check. "am checking" is the present continuous, for an action happening now; "checked" is past; "checking" cannot be the only verb of a sentence.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, technical) Hal and Linda put new tiles on the floor of their recreation room. Which form completes the sentence? "Hal spreads the mastic and Linda ___ the tiles."
questions.explanation: The two actions are joined by "and" and told in the same tense: "Hal spreads" is the present simple, so Linda places, with -s for a singular subject. "place" forgets the -s; "placing" needs be before it; "placed" changes the tense in the middle of the sentence.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2010, technical) A text presents Tanni Grey-Thomson, a famous wheelchair racer. Which form completes the sentence? "She is very serious about her sport, and so she ___ hard. She does 150 kilometres every week."
questions.explanation: "She does 150 kilometres every week" shows a routine, told in the present simple. The subject is "she", so the verb takes -s: trains. "train" forgets the -s; "training" has no auxiliary; "trained" is past, but the text describes how she works now.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) A guard at the Tower of London looks smart in his uniform and answers the visitors' questions. Which form completes the sentence? "He looks very smart in his well-known uniform, and of course, tourists ___ photos of him."
questions.explanation: The sentence tells what happens every day at the Tower, so the present simple is used. "tourists" is plural: the verb takes no -s, take. "takes" is the form for a singular subject; "taking" needs be before it; "are take" puts be in front of a base verb, where be needs a verb in -ing.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2001) The same guard has a difficult job but likes it. Which form completes the sentence? "He has a difficult job, but he likes it because he ___ people from all over the world."
questions.explanation: He likes his job because of something that happens all the time: present simple, like "likes". "he" is singular, so the verb takes -s: meets. "meet" forgets the -s; "meeting" needs be before it; "met" is past, whereas the job is a present fact.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2006) Dave and Jenny are old friends and neighbours, and it is time to say goodbye. Which form completes the sentence? "Now, Dave ___ because he found a new job in another city."
questions.explanation: "Now" and the goodbye show an action happening at this very moment: present continuous, be + verb in -ing, is leaving. "leaves" is the present simple, for a habit or a timetable; "are leaving" uses a plural auxiliary with a singular subject; "left" is past, which contradicts "Now".
